- [Substack: Private Credit Cracks, The AI "Boogeyman" & Why Crypto is for Boomers | The Real Eisman Playbook Episode 49](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/private-credit-cracks-the-ai-boogeyman-f80) - 2026-03-09

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Eisman, Glenn Schorr and Dwight Collins distinguish private-credit losses from fundraising pressure, debate software disruption and favor durable payments networks. The senior-debt cushion argument is conditionally valid, but current equity valuations and refinancing capacity remain unverified. Later Blue Owl filings show meaningful repayments, worsening residual credit metrics and continued parent fundraising. The dialogue reverses the public/private Blue Owl merger entities. Visa operating resilience is supported, while permanent immunity, price-causality and cross-asset incompatibility claims are overstated.

Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.

### 003. After a long benign period, losses doubling from a low base may be normalization rather than the start of a severe credit crisis.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | analytical principle | major

[Source at 4:30-5:35](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0Hqtxmb61A&t=270s) | Stance: endorsed | Horizon: not stated

Assume a loss rate rises from 1% to 2%. Relative increase is 100%, but the absolute change is one percentage point; neither calculation determines whether it subsequently rises to 10%. Need levels and trajectory, not percentage growth alone.

Conditional reasoning: Assume a loss rate rises from 1% to 2%. Relative increase is 100%, but the absolute change is one percentage point; neither calculation determines whether it subsequently rises to 10%. Need levels and trajectory, not percentage growth alone.

<a id="V0Hqtxmb61A-c004"></a>
### 004. Blue Owl proposed moving a small public BDC into a larger private BDC whose assets traded at a discount, imposing roughly a 20% haircut.

**Wrong** | Steve Eisman | explanation | supporting

[Source at 5:40-7:02](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0Hqtxmb61A&t=340s) | Stance: asserted | Horizon: not stated

The proposed direction was nontraded OBDC II into publicly traded OBDC. Discount was on listed shares versus NAV, not automatically a 20% markdown of underlying loans. The investor-value concern can be real despite reversed structure.

Qualification: Eisman corrects trillion to billion; preserve the correction rather than scoring the slip.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated obdc merger structure proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

- [OBDC and OBDC II merger agreement announcement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655888/000119312525267102/d93879dex991.htm) (2025-11-05): OBDC, the publicly traded NYSE fund, was to survive and issue shares to OBDC II investors. This contradicts the interview reversal of public and private entities. Listed-share discount and loan asset impairment are different concepts.

- [Blue Owl Capital Corporation II Q3 2026 Form 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1655887/000165588726000025/obdc-20260930.htm) (2026-11-06): Capital distributions through October totaled $4.16/share, about 50.3% of December 2025 NAV. September non-accruals were 10.4% at cost and 2.7% at fair value versus 3.1% and 1.4% in December; portfolio shrank materially. Repayment progress coexists with worsening credit composition; full recovery is unproven.

<a id="V0Hqtxmb61A-c013"></a>
### 013. Sponsor equity is junior to senior debt, so enterprise-value losses first consume equity before impairing the lender under a simple capital stack.

**Right** | Steve Eisman | explanation | major

[Source at 14:18-16:01](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0Hqtxmb61A&t=858s) | Stance: endorsed | Horizon: not stated

Assume one senior debt claim D, junior equity, no priming liabilities or bankruptcy costs, and realizable asset value V. Debt recovers min(D,V), equity max(V-D,0). Equity absorbs falling V until V<D. Original equity contribution does not guarantee current realizable value.

Conditional reasoning: Assume one senior debt claim D, junior equity, no priming liabilities or bankruptcy costs, and realizable asset value V. Debt recovers min(D,V), equity max(V-D,0). Equity absorbs falling V until V<D. Original equity contribution does not guarantee current realizable value.

Assessment test: Establish whether the stated equity first loss proposition holds using matched primary disclosures; retain its conditions and separate causal explanations from price movements.

## Framework and tools

- Separate manager equity, fund liquidity, loan credit and sponsor equity.
- Check realizable enterprise value and refinancing, not just original equity contribution.
- Challenge AI displacement by examining customer integration and workflow.
- Use credit spreads as a comparison signal, not proof that unrelated equities must be mispriced.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Blue Owl BDC merger and asset-sale waterfall
- Senior debt/equity numeric example
- High-yield spreads and HYG screen
- SoFi ABS cumulative-loss trigger
- Bank M&A regulatory window
- Payments business-model comparison

## Source cautions

Glenn Schorr handles private markets and credit; Dwight Collins covers investor sentiment, brokers, payments and SoFi. Turn-taking inferred from named prompts. Host closing explicitly adopts selected points; other guest forecasts remain separate.
- Public and private entities are reversed in the merger discussion; filing resolves the error.
- Recording predates publication: last week references February Blue Owl transaction.
- CQS insurer name is uncertain ASR, likely Kuvare.
- Guest loan-to-value near 35% becomes about 25% debt in host closing; neither treated as verified industry aggregate.
